title: Main loop invariant of the generator
statement: Let $c,C,q$ be natural numbers with $q>0$, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and choose a loop level $i<c+1$. Suppose the work-head positions are given by $h : \text{Fin}(c+1) \to \mathbb{Z}$, with every head at a level at most $i$ at position $0$. For $j,r\in\mathbb{N}$ with $j+r=q$ and any output word $o$, start in loop state $i$ with head $i$ at position $j$ and all other heads at their positions in $h$. After exactly $r\bigl(T_i+2\bigr)+q+2$ steps, where $T_i$ is the recursively defined cost for $i$ loop levels, the machine is in advance state $i+1$, the head positions are given by $h$, and the output is $o$ followed by $rCq^i$ ones.
hypotheses_covered: $h$ assigns integer positions to all work heads
Every head at a level at most $i$ has position $0$ in $h$
replaced:
Let $q > 0$ be the unary side length, let $i \le c$ be a loop level, and
suppose every head at a level $\le i$ is at displacement $0$ except that head
$i$ sits at $j$, where $j + r = q$. Then exactly $r\,(T_i + 2) + q + 2$ steps
(with $T_i$ the exact level-$i$ nest cost) execute the remaining $r$
iterations of loop $i$, append $r \cdot C q^i$ ones to the output, reset head
$i$ to $0$, and enter the advance state of level $i+1$; heads above level $i$
are arbitrary and remain unchanged.
